external_cause.operator_report: an outbound application firewall on the host prompted for and blocked the executor's provider connections during the previous series, and was to be configured to permit them
external_cause.what_this_repository_can_check: not the firewall's configuration — only whether the route works from the same executable, provider, model and credential the qualification will use

kind: boundary reassessment and provider-route readiness, before the requalification

notification_allowance.answer: none that the evidence shows. Two real trajectories — 27 model calls over 49 tool calls, and 26 over 53 — started and ran to completion under the boundary that did not have it. The allowance was introduced while a hang was being chased, and the hang appeared under the boundary that already had it.
notification_allowance.field_test: what required capability becomes impossible without it?
notification_allowance.identity_note: the selected policy expresses the same enforced profile as the boundary those trajectories ran under; its digest differs only because the rule's payload gained a field, which is off

transient_hang.not_concluded: that the firewall was definitely the cause on any particular attempt; the repository cannot see it, and says only what it measured
transient_hang.observed: one in-boundary probe timed out at 240 s; a host-side probe with the same executor, model and effort then succeeded in 3.9 s, and three in-boundary probes immediately afterwards — with and without a working directory, with and without a staged arm — each succeeded in about 3 s
transient_hang.reading: transient, and consistent with intermittent external interruption rather than with a boundary defect: the same boundary succeeds seconds later under the same configuration
